Rashi on Pesachim 49b:10:1.english: As though he had sexual relations with his betrothed in his presence - For he embarrasses him.

Rashi on Pesachim 49b:10:2.english: Betrothed - To all the congregations of Jacob.

Rashi on Pesachim 49b:11:1.hebrew: שנה ופירש - תלמיד ששנה ופירש מן התורה, ויודע כמה תלמידי חכמים מגנים את עמי הארץ וכמה הם שפלים בעיניהם, שונא יותר מכולם:
Rashi on Pesachim 49b:11:1.english: One who studied and separated - A student who studied and separated from the Torah, and knows how much Torah scholars disparage ignoramuses and how lowly they are in their eyes, hates [Torah scholars] more than all of them.

Rashi on Pesachim 49b:12:1.english: One does not entrust him with testimony - One does not summon him to hear a matter to testify about it.

Rashi on Pesachim 49b:12:2.hebrew: ואין מגלין לו סוד - שום דבר סתר, לפי שהולך רכיל ומגלה:
Rashi on Pesachim 49b:12:2.english: And one does not reveal a secret to him - Any hidden matter, because he goes about as a talebearer and reveals [it].

Rashi on Pesachim 49b:12:3.english: Over orphans - Because he is suspected of robbery.

Rashi on Pesachim 49b:12:4.hebrew: המוצא אבידה חייב להכריז - כדאמרי' באלו מציאות (ב"מ כא.), ועם הארץ לאו אחיך הוא, דאינו עושה מעשה עמך:
Rashi on Pesachim 49b:12:4.english: One who finds a lost item is obligated to announce [it] - As we say in [the chapter] Eilu Metziot (Bava Metzia 21a), and an ignoramus [am ha'aretz] is not [considered] "your brother," for he does not act [in accordance with] the deeds of your people.

Rashi on Pesachim 49b:15:1.hebrew: מזמנין - שלשה שאכלו כאחת, דתנן: חייבין לזמן ואין רשאין ליחלק:
Rashi on Pesachim 49b:15:1.english: They join in a zimmun (mezamnin) - Three [people] who ate together, as we learned in a Mishnah: "They are obligated to join in a zimmun, and they are not permitted to separate."

Rashi on Pesachim 49b:17:1.english: And you shall eat and be satisfied - From this verse we derive the blessing of (zimmun) in Berakhot (48b).

Rashi on Pesachim 49b:18:1.hebrew: חזרתו - ומדרבנן היא, ואשיעור טומאתו אסמכוה, וטומאת אוכלין בכביצה:
Rashi on Pesachim 49b:18:1.english: His returning - And it is by rabbinic decree, and they based it on the measure of its ritual impurity, and the ritual impurity of foods is [the size of] an egg-bulk.

Rashi on Pesachim 49b:1:1.english: And unacceptable - to those who hear [of it].

Rashi on Pesachim 49b:2:1.english: Great [people] of the generation - Men of [good] deeds and righteous people.

Rashi on Pesachim 49b:2:2.english: The daughter of charity collectors - For they do not appoint [them] unless [they are] good and trustworthy.

Rashi on Pesachim 49b:2:3.english: Their wives [are] a creeping animal - For they are not careful with the commandments.

Rashi on Pesachim 49b:2:4.english: With any animal - For they are similar to an animal, as they have no heart to understand.

Rashi on Pesachim 49b:5:1.english: For it is your life and the length of your days; he is not concerned about his own life - [that is, he does not care] to study Torah and live.

Rashi on Pesachim 49b:5:2.english: Regarding his fellow's life, all the more so - And there is [reason] to be concerned lest he kill him.

Rashi on Pesachim 49b:6:1.hebrew: ומגבו - דתו לא חיי, כדאמרינן בשחיטת חולין (דף כא:): קרעו כדג — מטמא באהל מיד, ואף על גב שמפרפר; ואמר רבי שמואל בר רב יצחק: ומגבו:
Rashi on Pesachim 49b:6:1.english: And from his back - For he can no longer live, as we say in Shechitat Chullin (21b): "[If] one tore him like a fish, he imparts impurity in a tent immediately, even though he is [still] convulsing"; and Rabbi Shmuel bar Rav Yitzchak said: "And from his back."

Rashi on Pesachim 49b:9:1.hebrew: אילמלא צריכין אנו להם - למזונותיהן ולעזרתם, היו הורגין אותנו:
Rashi on Pesachim 49b:9:1.english: If we did not need them - For their sustenance and for their assistance, they would kill us.

Tosafot on Pesachim 49b:12:1.hebrew: ויש אומרים אף אין מכריזין על אבידתו - וא"ת: מאין יודע שהיא של ע"ה? ואור"י: כגון ששיירא של ע"ה עוברת, וראינו שנפל מהם. והשתא משמע דדוקא אין מכריזין על אבידתו, אבל לגזול בידים לא — אע"ג דלית ליה האי סברא דבסמוך: אפשר דנפיק מיניה ברא מעליא. ותימה לר"י: אמאי ממונו אסור? השתא גופו מותר — שמותר לקורעו כדג — ממונו לא כל שכן? דכה"ג אמר בהגוזל בתרא (ב"ק קיט.) ובע"ז (דף כו.) גבי מוסר, למאן דלית ליה סברא דאפשר דנפיק מיניה ברא מעליא. ונר' לר"י דלעיל מיירי במכיר וכופר להכעיס, דה"ל הריגתו כמו פיקוח נפש, שהוא לסטין וחשוד על הדמים; דאי לאו הכי, היאך מותר להורגו ביום הכפורים שחל להיות בשבת? הלא אפילו נכרי אסור! וכן משמע הלשון "על חייו אינו חס", דמכיר וכופר; דיש הרבה עניני ע"ה, כדמוכח בסוטה בפ' היה נוטל (סוטה דף כב.). ואור"י דמה שאנו מקבלים עדות מע"ה, כדאמר בפרק חומר בקדש (חגיגה כב.): "כמאן מקבלים האידנא סהדותא מע"ה? כרבי יוסי":
Tosafot on Pesachim 49b:12:1.english: And there are those who say: One does not even announce their lost [items] - And if you ask: How does [the finder] know that it belongs to an ignoramus? And Rabbi Yitzchak says: [It refers to a case] such as where a caravan of ignoramuses is passing by, and we saw that it fell from them. And now it is implied that specifically one does not announce his lost item, but to steal [from him] directly is not [permitted] — even though [this opinion] does not hold that reasoning [mentioned] nearby [in the Gemara]: perhaps upstanding offspring will come from him. And it is astonishing to Rabbi Yitzchak: Why is his property forbidden [to be stolen]? Now [that] his body is permitted [to be harmed] — for it is permitted to tear him apart like a fish — is his property not all the more so [permitted]? For similarly [the Gemara] says in HaGozel Batra (Bava Kamma 119a) and in Avodah Zarah (26a) regarding an informer, according to the one who does not hold the reasoning that perhaps upstanding offspring will come from him. And it appears to Rabbi Yitzchak that [the Gemara] above is speaking of one who recognizes [the truth] and denies [it] out of spite, so that killing him is like saving a life, for he is a bandit and suspected of bloodshed; for if not so, how is it permitted to kill him on Yom Kippur that falls on Shabbat? Is not even [killing] a gentile forbidden [then]? And so too the wording "he does not spare his life" implies that he recognizes [the truth] and denies [it]; for there are many categories of ignoramuses, as is proven in Sotah in the chapter Hayah Notel (Sotah 22a). And Rabbi Yitzchak says that [the reason] we [nevertheless] accept testimony from an ignoramus [nowadays] is as [the Gemara] says in the chapter Chomer BaKodesh (Chagigah 22a): "In accordance with whom do we accept testimony nowadays from an ignoramus? In accordance with Rabbi Yosei."

Tosafot on Pesachim 49b:17:1.hebrew: ואכלת זו אכילה - נראה דהני שיעורי כזית וכביצה דלא הוי אלא אסמכתא, וכן פ"ה בפרק מי שמתו (ברכות כ:) גבי הא דאמר: בן מברך לאביו, ומוקי לה כגון דאכל האב שיעור דרבנן, ופ"ה שם דהיינו כזית וכביצה, דמדאורייתא בעינן שביעה גמורה. וכן מוכח התם דקאמר: "לא אשא פנים לישראל, שכתבתי להם: 'ואכלת ושבעת וברכת', והן מדקדקים על עצמם בכזית וכביצה". וקשה, דבפרק ג' שאכלו (שם מח.) אמר: ינאי מלכא ומלכתא כרכי ריפתא בהדי הדדי, אמר: מאן יהיב לן גברא דמברך לן? אייתוהו לרבי שמעון בן שטח וכו', שתה ובריך להו, וקאמר רבי שמעון בן שטח לגרמיה הוא דעבד, דלעולם אינו מוציא אחרים ידי חובה עד שיאכל כזית דגן. משמע דאם אכל כזית דגן, היה מוציא אחרים! ואי כזית דרבנן, היכי מפיק להו? הא אמר דלא אתי דרבנן ומפיק דאורייתא! ואור"י דהיינו דוקא קטן אינו מוציא אותו שאכל שיעור דאורייתא, אבל גדול — אפילו לא אכלי כלל, יכול להוציא אחרים מדאורייתא:
Tosafot on Pesachim 49b:17:1.english: "And you shall eat" — that is eating - It appears that these measurements of an olive-bulk and an egg-bulk are merely an asmakhta [a scriptural support for a rabbinic enactment]. And so Rashi explained in the chapter [entitled] Mi Shemeito (Berakhot 20b), regarding that which [the Mishnah] states: "A son may recite the blessing for his father," and [the Gemara] establishes it as [a case] where the father ate a rabbinic measurement — and Rashi explained there that this means an olive-bulk or an egg-bulk, for by Torah law we require complete satisfaction. And this is likewise proven there, as [God] says: "Shall I not show favor to Israel, to whom I wrote, 'And you shall eat and be satisfied and bless [the Lord your God],' yet they are scrupulous with themselves [to bless even] over an olive-bulk or an egg-bulk?" And this is difficult: for in the chapter [entitled] Sheloshah She'akhlu (ibid., 48a), [the Gemara] relates: King Yannai and the queen were eating bread together; he said, "Who will bring us a man to recite the blessing for us?" They brought Rabbi Shimon ben Shetach, etc.; he drank [a cup of wine] and recited the blessing for them. And [the Gemara] states that what Rabbi Shimon ben Shetach did, he did for himself [i.e., his own case was unique], for in general one does not discharge others of their obligation unless he eats an olive-bulk of grain. This implies that if he had eaten an olive-bulk of grain, he would have discharged others [of their obligation]. Yet if an olive-bulk is [only] a rabbinic [requirement], how could he discharge them? Behold, [the Gemara] states [there] that a rabbinic [obligation] cannot come and discharge a Torah [obligation]! And R"I [Rabbeinu Yitzchak] says that this applies specifically [to a minor]: a minor cannot discharge one who ate a Torah-level measurement; however, an adult — even if he did not eat at all — can discharge others [of their obligation] by Torah law.

Tosafot on Pesachim 49b:2:1.hebrew: לא מצא בת גבאי צדקה ישא בת מלמדי תינוקות - משמע דגבאי צדקה עדיפי ממלמדי תינוקות, והא דאמר בפרק השותפין (ב"ב ח:): "והמשכילים יזהירו כזוהר הרקיע" — אלו גבאי צדקה, "ומצדיקי הרבים ככוכבים" — אלו מלמדי תינוקות; צ"ל דזוהר הרקיע עדיף מזוהר כוכבים:
Tosafot on Pesachim 49b:2:1.english: [If] he cannot find the daughter of charity collectors, he should marry the daughter of schoolteachers - This implies that charity collectors are superior to schoolteachers. And [as for] that which [the Gemara] states in chapter HaShutafin (Bava Batra 8b): "And the wise shall shine like the brightness of the firmament" [Daniel 12:3] — these are the charity collectors; "and those who turn the many to righteousness like the stars" — these are the schoolteachers; one must say that the brightness of the firmament is superior to the brightness of the stars.

Tosafot on Pesachim 49b:8:1.hebrew: מה ארי דורס ואוכל - פר"ת: דורס ואוכל ואין ממתין עד שתמות; אף עם הארץ אינו ממתין עד שתתפייס:
Tosafot on Pesachim 49b:8:1.english: "Just as a lion mauls and eats" - Rabbeinu Tam explained: [The lion] mauls and eats and does not wait until [its prey] dies; so too, an ignoramus does not wait until [his wife] is appeased.
